description: Advisories from `composer audit --locked` that this fork knowingly carries.
The gate (scripts/ci/composer-audit.sh) fails on any advisory NOT listed
here. That is the point: none of these versions is this fork's choice —
app/composer.json is upstream's bluespice/core and every affected package is
a transitive dependency of MediaWiki 1.43.5 / BlueSpice 5.1.4 — so a bare
audit would be red on every push and would be ignored within a week. What
is worth failing a push over is a NEW advisory, and that is what this
Entries marked ACTION REQUIRED are fixable, but only by re-vendoring an
upstream tree, which is docs/dev/upgrade-runbook.md, not a PR. Read them
at the start of every upgrade: they are the reason to take one.
This file cannot see: MediaWiki core (vendored source, not a composer
package — that is the release-watch job, Track B), the two frozen packages
(stripped from composer.lock — Track C, see VERSIONS.yml and SECURITY.md),
or any vendored extension that is not also a composer package.

firebase/php-jwt.why: Transitive dependency of mediawiki/oauth. CVE-2025-45769 (low) is fixed only in 7.0.0, a major bump that upstream MediaWiki 1.43 has not taken; this fork does not choose the version. Not reachable unless the OAuth extension is enabled, which this deployment does not enable.

guzzlehttp/guzzle.why: Pinned to exactly 7.9.2 by upstream's app/composer.json (bluespice/core). Every advisory is fixed in 7.12.1-7.15.1, so the fix is a re-vendor of upstream, not a lockfile edit here. Used server-side by shellbox, monolog and the OAuth path; no untrusted URL reaches it from wiki content.

guzzlehttp/psr7.why: Transitive dependency of guzzlehttp/guzzle, which upstream pins exactly. Moves only when guzzle moves.

mediawiki/maps.why: ACTION REQUIRED at the next upgrade. CVE-2026-52854 (high) is fixed in 12.1.3 and this tree vendors 11.0.1. Fixing it means re-vendoring the Maps extension, which is an upstream-tree change and belongs to the upgrade process, not to a CI gate. Recorded here so it cannot be forgotten.

phpoffice/phpspreadsheet.why: ACTION REQUIRED at the next upgrade — the worst entry in this file. Nine advisories including two critical, all fixed in 1.30.6 or later against the vendored 1.30.1. It parses user-uploaded spreadsheets for bluespice/uemoduletable2excel and mediawiki/data-transfer, so the input is genuinely untrusted wherever upload is permitted. Version chosen by upstream BlueSpice 5.1.4; fixed by re-vendoring.

phpseclib/phpseclib.why: ACTION REQUIRED at the next upgrade. Two high advisories, fixed in 3.0.54 against the vendored 3.0.48. It sits under jumbojett/openid-connect-php — the same library the security-critical oidc-client patch targets — so this is on the authentication path whenever OIDC login is configured.

phpunit/phpunit.why: Development-only: packages-dev, and docker/setup.sh installs with --no-dev, so it is not in the shipped vendor/ tree at all. CVE-2026-24765 cannot be reached by a wiki request.

psy/psysh.why: Development-only (packages-dev, --no-dev at install). It is MediaWiki's eval.php shell; reaching it already requires shell access to the container.

symfony/process.why: Transitive dependency pulled in by symfony/console and mwstake's process manager. CVE-2026-24739 (medium) is fixed in 6.4.33 against the vendored 6.4.31; the version is resolved by upstream's constraints.

symfony/yaml.why: Pinned to exactly 5.4.45 by upstream's app/composer.json. Three low stack-exhaustion advisories in the parser; the YAML this wiki parses is repo-controlled (pipeline and config files), not user input.

universal-omega/dynamic-page-list3.why: ACTION REQUIRED at the next upgrade. CVE-2025-53625 (high) exposes hidden/suppressed usernames and is fixed in 3.6.4; BlueSpice 5.1.4 vendors the 3.6.2.1+BlueSpice511 build. Relevant to any wiki that suppresses users, and fixed only by re-vendoring the extension.

web-auth/webauthn-lib.why: Low, and specific to SimpleFakeCredentialGenerator used with an empty secret — a username-enumeration hardening feature, not an authentication bypass. Fixed in 5.3.5; the vendored 4.9.2 comes with mediawiki/web-authn.
